title: Independently audit native equality-cut signs and caller contracts
body:
PR #5588 requested independent review of its signed stabilizer tariff and full-word/cached-history/endpoint contracts. This package checks `PROOF.md` §§3–5 at `97db3fb45cd93a350e300781d75440d14e6a1f73`: the claims hold under the stated cut-preserving hypotheses; no defect was found in that scope. A separate trace derivation makes the Pauli-sign cancellation explicit and proves the bound for arbitrary n, width, chronological feedback and complete initial availability J.

The independently written exact checks cover 366 signed ordered Pauli image frames (not all Clifford unitaries), 54 literal projectors, Bell-sign and inter-column endpoint controls, one 18-operation dirty-feedback word and all 19 prefixes, ten paid-update cases, joint cache rank and nonunitary code controls. In particular, duplicate cached responses have joint rank1 rather than2, and preserving cut rank alone does not preserve the unit error floor.

Validation: registered Python3.12 replay and isolated optimized replay; committed-byte/source-history checks; deterministic 13-file export and integrity check; fresh Git-free optimized replay with identical receipt; altered-source and altered-receipt rejection controls. See `research/native-equality-independent-audit/VERIFICATION.md`. Current main was refreshed before submission and remains the pinned base `df0137efd35e11b4445734bf612bdd4c7ebc330c`.

Scope excludes the source profile algorithm (§6), row-packing discussion (§7), actual P104 availability extraction, supplier/physical replay, and the full multiplication theorem. No κ improvement or frontier change; selected P104 κ=62009/20000000 retains its five premises. This is an agent-assisted independent derivation and implementation, not independent human or proof-kernel acceptance.

Canonical claim/handoff: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5582#discussioncomment-19188980
Original review request: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19183713

Ali Romman retains credit for the source theorem and its cached-boundary/endpoint limitations; classical rank/stabilizer theory and all source predecessor attribution are retained. New audit prepared for Hiroki KUMAZAKI with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including delegated proof, contract-check and sign review. Apache-2.0.
